newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., hires seaport adviser, auditor.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., hires seaport adviser, auditor.

text.p: MIAMI, June 9 (Rueter) - Florida's Dade County has hired Public Financial Managment Inc as outside financial adviser for the troubled Port of Miami, and appointed Ernst & Young LLP to conduct a special seaport audit.
Metro-Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas announced the appointments during the weekend.
"This represents the first step in our efforts to restore the credibility of port finances with the financial markets and the people of Dade County," Penelas said.
The county, which runs the seaport, discovered last month that the port had operating deficits in seven of the last 10 years and had borrowed $22 million from the county general fund.
Public Financial Management, based in Philadelphia, recently served as adviser to the state-appointed oversight board that guided the City of Miami out of a $68 milion budget deficit.
Penelas asked the firm to review the port's overall condition and the viability of the revenue projections that were presented to support a proposed $163 million seaport expansion project.
Ernst & Young, headquartered in Tuscon, Ariz., will work with a county-appointed financial oversight commmittee to develop financial countrol and accountability measures at the Port of Miami.
